solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female philanthropist's gripe about new player

indicators.note: one word goes round another, so the complaint wraps around the next item

parts.note: a beef is a complaint
N is the abbreviation for new
a female stage player

explanation.surface: A wealthy woman donor is grumbling about a newcomer in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: BE(N)EF + ACTRESS. The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who gives money or help to a cause, the feminine form of benefactor.

clue.text: Snag over scraps in animal shelters?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a bur is a prickly seed head that snags on clothing
scraps and rows are both quarrels

explanation.surface: Someone's clothing catches on something while scrapping animals fight in their pens.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: burrows are dug, not built, but they shelter rabbits and badgers.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrow is a hole or tunnel an animal digs to live in, so it serves as its shelter.

clue.text: Gullibility of first-class surgeon in New York

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: standard abbreviation
A1 means first-class, written with I for the one
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A patient trusts a top surgeon practising in New York a little too readily.
explanation.walkthrough: N(AI VET)Y. A1 for first-class is a crossword staple, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent lack of worldly experience, which leaves one easily fooled: gullibility.

clue.text: One who'll agitate, and sack musicians without resistance

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the group sits around the single letter

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A troublemaker dismisses the band, who put up no fight.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRE + BA(R)ND. 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its older sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a person who stirs up unrest or passionately champions a cause, an agitator.

clue.text: First of children at school taking English class

indicators.note: the opening letter of each following word is kept, an acrostic

parts.note: initials of the five words in turn

explanation.surface: A pupil is first among the children learning English in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' reaches across all five words, not just 'children'; the initials spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system, so the word means class.

clue.text: Deterioration concerning Scandinavian nomads, reportedly

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the people's name is turned into a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the Lapps are reindeer-herding people of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A report concerns some decline among the herding peoples of the Arctic north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lapps, now usually called the Sami, live in northern Scandinavia; RE plus a sound-alike of their name gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness or bad ways after improving, a deterioration.

clue.text: Southern girl receiving useful marks primarily for precis

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so letters go inside the name

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern

indicators.note: primarily points to the leading letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: first letters of the two words
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from the South earns decent marks mainly for her précis exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern girl' reads as one person, but the two letters go between the S and the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A precis is a short summary of a text, giving its main points in condensed form.

clue.text: Fellow at sea evidently holding city priest's office

indicators.note: holding means having something inside, so the city sits within the phrase

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
LA is Los Angeles
one at sea is evidently in a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor plainly keeps hold of the town clergyman's post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like 'confused', but it is literal: someone at sea is evidently aboard, in a ship. The city goes inside the fellow-plus-ship phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplainship is the post or tenure of a chaplain, a clergyman attached to an institution.

clue.text: Cross-country runner, one that disturbs a bird of prey
Note diving bird nibbling Mike's sage

parts.note: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a bird nibbling takes something into its mouth, so the bird surrounds the letter

parts.note: the loon is the North American name for the diver
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A diving bird is pecking at a herb belonging to Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: SO + LO(M)ON. 'Sage' looks like the herb, especially beside 'nibbling', but it is a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon, the biblical king, was famed for wisdom, so his name is used for any wise man or sage.

clue.text: Susceptible sort in Nantes for a change

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gullible type spends some time in the French city of Nantes for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Susceptible sort' reads as one phrase, but 'sort' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nonresistant means offering no resistance, so one is susceptible to infection or influence.

clue.text: Memorable saying for part of speech

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a verb is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: A well-turned phrase is selected for inclusion in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word, but it is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying, memorable and often quoted, stating a general truth.

clue.text: Give account of island in old map

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the island letter is placed inside the drawing

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to account for an island marked on an antique chart.
explanation.walkthrough: EX + PLA(I)N.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to give an account of it, describing it clearly or making it understood.

clue.text: Arsenic, for example, subject to analysis?

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
say means for example

explanation.surface: Arsenic, say, as a sample a chemist might test.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests arsenic is the thing being tested; really it supplies its symbol, and 'subject to analysis' is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay a metal or ore is to test it chemically to find its composition or purity.

clue.text: Extremely pretty teacher, astonishingly original

indicators.note: something done astonishingly is done in a surprising way, so the letters come out in a new order
extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A very attractive teacher is strikingly unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely pretty' reads as 'very pretty', but it means only the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original model or pattern from which copies are made, so it is the original.

clue.text: Weep over quiet chap initially misusing code name

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: to weep is to cry
p, piano, means quietly in music
a man's name

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the word keeps only its opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone cries about a quiet man who first misused a secret code name.
explanation.walkthrough: CRY + P + TONY + M. 'Chap' is any man's name; here Tony.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptonym is a secret name used to conceal identity, as with intelligence agents: a code name.

clue.text: Briefly drawing back, ultimately feel very mean

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the shortened word is read from right to left
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: dragging means drawing or pulling along

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each of the two words gives its final letter

parts.note: last letters of both words

explanation.surface: Pulling away at the last moment makes someone feel stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAGGIN(G) reversed, then L and Y. 'Drawing back' reads as one phrase meaning recoiling, but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Niggardly means stingy, unwilling to spend or give, which is one sense of mean.

clue.text: Travel runs badly: at the bottom of that is a primate

indicators.text: at the bottom of that is
indicators.note: in a down clue, at the bottom means the last piece goes beneath what comes before

parts.note: to go is to travel
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
taken as written

explanation.surface: Things go badly on a trip, and an ape is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: GO + R + ILL, with A placed underneath in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest of the great apes, and apes belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Not gregarious like spies in centre of Honolulu

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: the agency is placed inside the middle letters
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the two central letters are kept

parts.note: the fourth and fifth of its eight letters
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Secret agents in Hawaii's capital keep to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: AS + O(CIA)L.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding the company of others, the opposite of gregarious, which means sociable.

clue.text: Hindu sage's son with friend in Rouen

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
W is the abbreviation for with
ami is French for friend, and Rouen is in France

explanation.surface: An Indian holy man's son is visiting a friend in Normandy.
explanation.walkthrough: S + W + AMI. Naming a French city signals that a French word is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man, used as a title of respect.

clue.text: Inflammation principally suffered on a French stream

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: first letter
un is French for a
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: Someone got burnt sitting out beside a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: S + UN + BURN. A burn is a Scots and northern English word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunburn is reddening and inflammation of the skin caused by too much exposure to the sun.

clue.text: State supplying some practical geriatricians

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A government provides practical doctors who care for the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: practic(AL GERIA)tricians.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African country, a state in the sense of a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Expatiate tediously about old barbed missile

indicators.note: the phrase goes around the next letter

parts.note: to harp on is to go on and on about something
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone drones on endlessly about an old weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: HARP(O)ON. Expatiate means to speak at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired at whales or large fish, a barbed missile.

clue.text: Brought up part of joint composition

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tenon is the tongue that fits into a mortise in a woodworking joint

explanation.surface: A section of a jointly written piece is raised for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of joint' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is the definition of the word to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical composition for nine voices or instruments.

clue.text: Tense about performing in the near future

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word goes around the next one

parts.note: tense means taut, tight
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: A nervous actor waits to go on stage before tonight's show.
explanation.walkthrough: T(ON)IGHT. 'Tense' looks like the grammar term, a nice fit with 'in the near future', but it means taut.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening of the present day, which is coming soon, in the near future.

clue.text: Medication taken by one on bike seat

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist swallows a tablet before riding.
explanation.walkthrough: PILL + I + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is the passenger seat behind the rider on a motorcycle.

clue.text: Turn one out, identifying particle

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns a person away after picking out a tiny fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' is itself a common anagram signal, but here it is fodder and 'out' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge, found in the atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Wager involving everyone Asian having a passion for dance

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the bet wraps around the word for everyone

parts.note: a bet is a wager
all means everyone
an Omani is a person from Oman, in Asia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bet that everyone makes involves an Asian person mad keen on dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: B(ALL)ET + OMANI + A. 'A' looks part of the definition, but it supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Balletomania is an enthusiasm for ballet, combining ballet with mania, a passion or craze.
